The supplementary statement on the distribution of cancer diagnoses among acutely operated patients in Denmark between September 1, 2022, and August 31, 2023, provides a comprehensive breakdown of cancer types across regions and hospitals [^src1]. The data, sourced from the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]], reveals that the vast majority of operated patients in the country do not have a cancer diagnosis [^src1]. 

Out of 3,151 total operated patients nationally, 2,935 (93.15%) had no cancer diagnosis [^src1]. Gastrointestinal cancers accounted for 159 patients (5.05% of the national total), while other cancer diseases comprised 42 patients (1.33%), and gynecological cancers represented 15 patients (0.48%) [^src1]. Because this data represents a single reporting period, no longitudinal trends can be established from this table alone [^src1].

At the regional level, [[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]] led in total surgical volume, accounting for 1,095 operations (34.75% of the national total) [^src1]. [[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]] followed with 682 operations (21.64%) [^src1]. In contrast, [[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]] recorded the lowest volume among the five regions, with 270 operations (8.57%) [^src1]. 

At the hospital level, [[herlev-og-gentofte-hospital|Herlev og Gentofte Hospital]] performed the highest number of operations (306, or 9.71% of the national total) [^src1]. The lowest volumes were observed at [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]] with just 3 operations (0.10%) and [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] with 30 operations (0.95%) [^src1]. 

Several hospitals emerged as outliers by reporting zero cases across all tracked cancer categories. [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]], [[kolding-sygehus|Kolding Sygehus]], and [[odense-universitetshospital-svendborg|Odense Universitetshospital - Svendborg]] reported 0 gastrointestinal, 0 gynecological, and 0 other cancer diagnoses, meaning 100% of their operated patients fell into the "no cancer diagnosis" category [^src1]. Conversely, [[rigshospitalet|Rigshospitalet]] had a notably high proportion of its small surgical volume (58 patients) dedicated to non-cancer cases (53 patients, 1.68% of the national total), with suppressed data (`#`) for gastrointestinal cancers and zero gynecological cases [^src1]. [[aalborg-universitetshospital|Aalborg Universitetshospital]] also showed a significant concentration of gastrointestinal cancers, reporting 19 cases (0.60% of the national total) out of its 174 total operations [^src1].
